title: Resizable Panels component for React and Next.js
description: Build adjustable workspaces with horizontal and vertical panels, keyboard and pointer resizing, collapse/restore, constraints, and theme tokens.

intro: Compose adjustable workspaces with ResizablePanels, ResizablePanel, and ResizableHandle. Configure percentage limits and collapse behavior while keeping pane content and persistence in your application.
useCases: Code editors with preview and console panes.
Vertical tool panels on narrow screens.

faqs.question: How are panel sizes measured?
faqs.answer: Sizes are percentage shares of pane space, excluding resize handles. They total 100; dragging adjusts only the adjacent pair. Every panel has a stable DOM id.

faqs.question: What keyboard controls are available?
faqs.answer: Use Left/Right for horizontal layouts or Up/Down for vertical layouts. Shift increases the step by ten. Home/End move to the available limits; Enter collapses or restores the preceding collapsible pane.

faqs.question: Does a vertical layout require a height?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set a height on the group or place it inside a parent that establishes one. Panes scroll independently when their content exceeds the available space.

faqs.question: Can I save panel sizes?
faqs.answer: Use controlled sizes and onSizesChange in your own state. Save onResizeEnd to avoid writing on every pointer movement. The component does not access localStorage during server rendering.

faqs.question: What happens to collapsed content?
faqs.answer: Content remains mounted. A zero-sized pane is inert and hidden from assistive technology; a nonzero collapsed rail remains accessible.

faqs.question: What are the composition rules?
faqs.answer: Use direct alternating Panel, Handle, Panel children. Arrays and fragments are supported. Each nested group owns independent state. Expanded minima must total at most 100 and maxima at least 100; invalid composition or constraints throw an actionable error.

faqs.question: Does it need an animation dependency?
faqs.answer: No. The static entry uses React and native pointer capture. It respects horizontal RTL direction and supports mouse, pen, and touch.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Horizontal and vertical split layouts with controlled or uncontrolled percentages, per-panel bounds, collapse/restore, and independently themed panel and handle surfaces.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body: Handles expose focusable separator semantics, accessible labels, value bounds, and controls relationships. Keep panel IDs unique in the document and label each handle for its primary pane.
